gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI AC180 solar input is capped at 10 A. That cap means the AC180 + 2 × 200 W kit, which is in stock at $1,232, can only approach 400 W if its two SP200L panels are wired in series. BLUETTI's own AC180 manual gives no series or parallel instruction, and our page currently says the panels 'go in parallel'.
standout_why: I compared against StormWatts' brand-vs-third-party article, Powersized's solar-generator-kits page, Volt & Valley's combo guide and our own bundle page. StormWatts and Powersized both list the AC180 at 12–60 V and 10 A, but neither applies that to the 400 W kit. Volt & Valley says 2 × 220–250 W panels fit 'under the 500W ceiling' and never mentions amps. Our page says the AC180's panels go in parallel, which is wrong given the 10 A cap. None of these pages tells the shopper how to wire the two-panel kit, and none says the brand manual is silent on it.
decides: This confirms that the single-panel kits are the simpler buys: ALLPOWERS P1800 + SP037 and EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus + 400 W each plug one panel into one input. The AC180 + 2 × 200 W kit, priced at $1,232 on 2026-11-08, gets close to 400 W only when wired in series, and it is also the most expensive kit here. Our 'Takes all 400 W?' cell for the AC180 should change from 'Yes' to 'Only in series (10 A input cap)', and the line saying the panels go in parallel should be removed.

findings.label: Solar input current cap
findings.source_title: Brand vs Third-Party Solar Panels for Power Stations: Adapters, Warranty, and Real Cost | StormWatts
findings.note: StormWatts gives this as the AC180 limit and cites BLUETTI's AC180 FAQ. Powersized's kit page also lists '12 to 60V, 10A' with a DC7909 plug. I could not open a BLUETTI page carrying the 10 A figure (see unsourced).

findings.label: What the manual says about panel voltage and wiring
findings.value: Solar input DC 12–60 V; 'Do not use solar panels with open circuit voltage higher than 60V'; no instruction on series or parallel wiring; no amp figure
findings.note: The voltage limit and warning are on manual p.3, and troubleshooting on p.20 repeats 12–60 VDC (error E033 is PV overvoltage). Arithmetic: 400 W ÷ 10 A = 40 V operating voltage needed. Parallel panels run at one panel's voltage. A pair that stays under 60 V Voc in series needs each panel under 30 V Voc, so its operating voltage is below 30 V. Wired in parallel, such a pair is capped below 30 V × 10 A = 300 W. So the kit can only approach 400 W in series.
